intro: Lesson 17: The Khulafa ar-Rashidun and Abu Bakr as the first caliph. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: A day of sadness
points: The Prophet ﷺ died in 632 CE
Abu Bakr calmed everyone with the truth

panels.title: Choosing the leader
points: He was the Prophet's ﷺ closest friend

keywords.def: successor: the leader of the Muslims after the Prophet ﷺ

questions.q: Explain why the Companions chose Abu Bakr.
questions.a: He was the Prophet's ﷺ closest companion, truthful, had led the prayers in the Prophet's ﷺ illness, and was chosen by consultation.

questions.q: Put in order: Uthman, Abu Bakr, Ali, Umar.

Make a caliph fact file for Abu Bakr on the pupil PDF (title, dates, how chosen, one quality), then write in the portal response box why his speech mattered. Start: 'Abu Bakr's words mattered because ...'
questions.a: Accurate fact file; speech kept Muslims focused on worshipping Allah alone
Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger; messengers before him died; Islam continues.

questions.q: Stretch: why is shura a good way to choose a leader?
questions.a: People discuss, share wisdom and agree together.
A) Umar ibn al-Khattab. The order is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali.

questions.q: Think again: what did the community need, and how did Abu Bakr help?
questions.a: Calm, truth and a trusted leader: he reminded them Allah is alive.
